Done. The pruned checkpoint is written and verified.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T2/solution.py`, a plain safetensors plus torch script. It builds one keep-index that drops the 64-wide block of head 5, applies it to each of the three 768-wide q/k/v segments of the fused projection columns and bias, and to the rows of the output projection.
- Ran it once. It succeeded on the first execution and wrote `out/T2/model.safetensors`.
- Wrote `out/T2/REPORT.md` with the self-report fields.

**Checks the script enforces before writing**

- Input and output tensor count of 160, identical key set, no pre-existing destination.
- Per-layer input and output shapes on all 36 touched tensors, dtypes unchanged.
- The four required checks from TASK.md on layer 0.
- Layer 0 values equal the concatenation of the exact column and row ranges listed in the task.
- Every untouched tensor is bit-equal to the input, and the file is reloaded and compared bit-exactly after saving.

**Independent verification**

A hand-written attention forward in float64 showed the pruned 11-head weights produce exactly the same output as the original 12-head weights with head 5 zeroed, in all 12 layers. The maximum difference was 0.0.

**Pitfalls worth noting**

- The `prune_heads` route suggested in the allowed-packages list does not exist in transformers 5.12.1. The method has been removed.
- Transformers' GPT-2 attention derives head size from hidden size divided by head count, so it cannot instantiate an 11-head model with 704-wide projections. A transformers-based functional check was therefore impossible, which is why I used the manual forward.
- The mask buffer named `attn.bias` shares a prefix with the real biases, so selection keys on `c_attn.bias`.
